title: Pin what a picture model can't keep
statement: When a model makes pictures or film, fix each recurring character, place and medium once per unit with a reused reference, since it has no memory between pictures.
detail: Among eight lessons one QC day in the reading project made standing practice: the model cannot count objects in generated art unless the scene line enumerates exactly how many, and recurring locations and mediums drift unless they are pinned (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0213-qc-week-0902-0904.qmd`). Research for the Grade 9 lessons found that the comics failure readers don't forgive is a character whose face, hair or proportions shift between panels, because diffusion generation has no memory across calls unless it is deliberately conditioned on a reference (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0249-g9-idea-research-full-files.qmd`). Also give the exact number of each object in the scene line, because the model can't count.
against: The cross-panel evidence is practitioner reports, though the research file calls its mechanism, no memory across calls, a verifiable technical fact (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0249-g9-idea-research-full-files.qmd`). The rule rests on the document's claim that recognition should replace recap in a story told in parts, which it calls its thinnest: nobody has tested recognition against recap for a child who has forgotten the earlier part (`downloads/BrainLift - What makes a good intro video.md`, line 62).
